newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tropical storm Andres picking up steam off Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Tropical storm Andres picking up steam off Mexico.

text.p: Tropical storm Andres, the first weather system of this year's hurricane season, is picking up steam and closing in on Mexico's Pacific Coast, weather sources said Tuesday.
"Andres is getting closer to the coast" a weather forecaster for TV network Televisa said. "By the evening it will be affecting the port of Huatulco," he added.
The storm, packing sustained winds of 40 mph (65 km/h) and gusts of 53 mph (85 km/h), was 147 miles (235 km) south of the Oaxaca at dawn, National Weather Service said.

In an update, the service said Andres was moving north, northeast at five mph (8 km/h) and estimated that by 1300 local/1800 GMT it would be 119 miles (190 km) south of the Oaxacan port of Puerto Angel. Sea swells of up to four meters were reported, it added.
"Extreme warnings go out to all shipping around the Gulf of Tehuantepec," the service said. It gave no indication if the system would be upgraded to a hurricane.

Televisa's weather forecaster said the storm would bring strong winds to the key coffee-producing states of Chiapas and Oaxaca and would also affect states farther to the north along Mexico's Pacific coast, namely Jalisco and Michoacan. Jalisco is the country's top corn-growing state.
"It is heading north, towards Chiapas and Oaxaca, and will probably bring a lot of rains to those states," the forecaster said.
